messages:
maya: quick RFC follow-up: i sketched a small edge shim to compact repeated span attributes inside a single bundle before we envelope+write. idea is to reduce bytes/index churn for high-volume services. link: https://rfd/internal/obs/compact-bundle (summary below)

jon: curious how "compaction" works in practice. are we mutating customer payloads?

maya: no. we only rewrite our internal envelope at the gateway layer (short-lived). we pull identical k/v pairs that appear across multiple spans in a bundle up into a coalesced map and leave per-span overrides. downstream can either expand or query against both maps.

sam: main wins = less egress + lower index cardinality, right?

maya: yep. also fewer index writes for common keys. tradeoffs: 1) late-enrich flows need deterministic rehydrate rules, 2) some legacy query patterns might require index-time expansion.

liz: show a tiny before/after?

maya: example (pseudo):

```json
{"spans":[
  {"id":"a","attrs":{"svc":"billing","region":"us-west1","user":"u1"}},
  {"id":"b","attrs":{"svc":"billing","region":"us-west1","user":"u1"}},
  {"id":"c","attrs":{"svc":"billing","region":"us-west1","user":"u2"}}
]}
```
becomes
```json
{"coalesced":{"svc":"billing","region":"us-west1"},
 "per_span":[{"id":"a","attrs":{"user":"u1"}},{"id":"b","attrs":{"user":"u1"}},{"id":"c","attrs":{"user":"u2"}}]
}
```

maya: coalesced map acts as defaults; per_span overrides win.

jon: ok for low-card keys. we must blacklist high-cardinality/PII from coalescing (user, request_id, email). how do we decide programmatically?

maya: proposed rules: three buckets. always_coalesce = explicit low-cardinality keys we control (svc, region, env), never_coalesce = explicit PII/high-card keys, adaptive = coalesce if same value appears in >=M spans in bundle AND global-cardinality for that key is under a rate threshold. defaults in RFC: M=3, global-cardinality < 2000/minute for that key.

sam: billing attribution: we currently resolve billing_key by scanning span attrs at sample time. if we move billing_key into coalesced area, parity must be preserved.

maya: contract: shim will synthesize a billing_key present on each per_span when downstream expects it. normalization pass ensures pipelines that read per-span attrs see identical billing_key values as before.

liz: validation approach?

jon: run dual ingest for a canary window: accept both raw and compacted envelopes, compute metrics: billing_parity_rate, query_delta_count, bytes_saved_pct, index_write_delta. rollback if billing_parity_rate > 0.1% or query_delta_count too high.

ingest-bot: canary pipeline created: ingest-compact-canary. runner job scheduled.

maya: rollout plan: prototype locally -> staging test with full diff harness 48h -> us-west canary 10% 7d -> widen if diffs < thresholds and bytes_saved > 5%. backoff on any billing/parity signal.

sam: consider sampling interactions. if sampling drops spans, coalescing at ingress must use the full bundle before sampling so sampled outputs keep same semantics. otherwise we risk hiding attributes on unsampled spans.

maya: agreed. derive coalesced state from full bundle before sampling filter. we must also ensure partial-bundle cases are handled deterministically (if bundle trimmed, fall back to noop compaction).

jon: index-time options: either expand coalesced map at index-write (cheaper for query compatibility) or change query engine to read coalesced maps. i prefer index-time expansion to minimize query changes. will POC expansion in the indexer.

liz: index-time expansion adds CPU, but keeps queries intact. also add a telemetry flag `ingest.compacted_v1=true/false` on records so we can trace regressions.

maya: perf target for shim: median added latency < 2ms on edge path; fail-open if >5ms. aim for >=6% stored-byte savings for high-churn services.

jon: edge cases: mixed-values where most spans share a value but one differs. our schema must make overrides explicit. also log the first N mismatches per service in debug-mode.

sam: owner matrix?

maya: proposed: jon -> shim prototype + tests, sam -> diff harness + billing parity suite, liz -> index-write expansion POC, maya -> rollout + policy finalization.

ingest-bot: actions created: jon assigned shim-proto, sam assigned parity-harness, liz assigned index-poc, maya assigned reviewer. due: 2026-04-05

jon: i'll start a repo tree `ingest/edge/compact_shim/` and a README describing `--mode=sample|rewrite|noop` and `--rules-file` format. will add sample bundles and unit tests.

maya: add a feature flag so we can flip per-service. also keep a short lived copy of raw envelopes for 72h during canary for forensic parity checks.

liz: also add a dry-run telemetry stream that emits what would have been coalesced (size + keys) without changing pipeline. helps tune rules.

sam: +1. let's sync next Wed morning. thanks all. :thumbsup:
